lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Jets score on first 5 drives and edge Chargers 27-24 to snap 5-game skid
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: INGLEWOOD, Calif.  -- — Mired in a losing season, New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith 's efficiency has been largely overlooked with the offense lagging.  Sterling Shepard helped change that Sunday, catching two touchdown passes from Smith and potentially earning himself a permanent promotion.  Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and another TD as the Jets scored on their first five drives to beat the Los Angeles Chargers 27-24 and end a five-game skid.

injuryReport.name: Drake Maye
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

injuryReport.name: A.J. Brown
injuryReport.beatComment: Coming out of a Week 11 bye, Brown didn't take any reps during the two bonus practices the Patriots held Monday and Tuesday, so it comes as little surprise that he was absent from the team's first official practice of Week 12. Head coach Mike Vrabel has already acknowledged that Brown isn't expected to play Sunday versus the Chargers, but the Patriots will likely wait until after Friday's practice before officially ruling the receiver out for that contest.

injuryReport.name: Walter Rouse
factors: Remains in early stages of NFL 5-Step Concussion Protocol
injuryReport.beatComment: Rouse is in the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing in Week 10 against the Lions in Munich. Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice. Even if he practices over the coming days, an independent neurologist would need to clear Rouse from protocol in order for him to be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

injuryReport.name: Carlton Davis III
injuryReport.beatComment: Davis didn't travel with the Patriots to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. Even with the extra rest courtesy of the bye, Davis has not been cleared by medical staff to return to practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a realistic shot of playing Sunday against the Chargers.

injuryReport.name: Alijah Vera-Tucker
factors: 21-day IR window open (Week 1 ramp); returned to Limited Participation (LP) Wednesday
Requires formal 53-man roster activation prior to weekly NFL transaction deadline
injuryReport.beatComment: The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.

injuryReport.name: Romeo Doubs
factors: 21-day IR window open (Week 1 ramp); returned to Limited Participation (LP) Wednesday
Requires formal 53-man roster activation prior to weekly NFL transaction deadline
injuryReport.beatComment: According to Mike Reiss of ESPN.com, Doubs did individual drills and ran routes against air, suggesting the wide receiver was especially limited after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the day. Doubs looks genuinely questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

injuryReport.beatComment: Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

injuryReport.name: Ben Brown
factors: Beat/podium consensus: on track to suit up
injuryReport.beatComment: Brown did not play in the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Lions in Munich due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. With a full practice under his belt, Brown is on track to play against the Chargers on Sunday and should reclaim his starting spot at left guard while Walter Rouse reverts to a depth role on the offensive line.

coachingMatchup.headline: Jim Harbaugh & DC Chris O'Leary vs. HC Mike Vrabel, OC Josh McDaniels & DC Zak Kuhr (SoFi Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Los Angeles Chargers's staff (Jim Harbaugh, OC Mike McDaniel, DC Chris O'Leary) against New England Patriots (5-5)—testing both Los Angeles's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress New England Patriots's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against New England Patriots's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Chris O'Leary balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Los Angeles sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to New England Patriots's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: SoFi Stadium situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: DJ Uiagalelei, Charlie Kolar & Quentin Johnston vs. S Craig Woodson & LB Elijah Ponder
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAC: #29 Pass Off (164.7 yds) · #32 Off. Scoring (-7.58) | NE: #27 Pass Def (+4.59)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: DJ Uiagalelei, Charlie Kolar & Quentin Johnston attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against New England Patriots's #27 pass defense (+4.59). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Los Angeles's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch DJ Uiagalelei (#7) scanning Patriots's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Elijah Ponder widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Charlie Kolar (#88).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Teair Tart, Jamaree Caldwell & Dalvin Tomlinson vs. QB Tommy DeVito & OT Will Campbell
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAC: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | NE: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Teair Tart, Jamaree Caldwell & Dalvin Tomlinson lead Los Angeles's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against New England Patriots's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Chargers keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Teair Tart (#93) draw chip help from Patriots's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Jamaree Caldwell (#99).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Tarheeb Still, Cam Hart & Tuli Tuipulotu vs. WR Mack Hollins & QB Tommy DeVito
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAC: #22 Pass Def (+3.48) | NE: #13 Pass Off (233.6 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Tarheeb Still, Cam Hart & Tuli Tuipulotu anchor Los Angeles's #22 pass defense (+3.48) against WR Mack Hollins and New England Patriots's #13 passing attack (233.6 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Patriots into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Tarheeb Still (#4) at the top of routes against WR Mack Hollins: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Tommy DeVito's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Omarion Hampton & Scott Matlock vs. Patriots Front Seven & LB Elijah Ponder
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAC: #10 Rush Off (123.4 yds) | NE: #16 Rush Def (-0.63)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Omarion Hampton & Scott Matlock test New England Patriots's #16 run defense (-0.63) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Patriots's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Patriots's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Omarion Hampton (#8).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jake Slaughter, Joe Alt & Cole Strange vs. DT Christian Barmore & Patriots Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAC: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | NE: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jake Slaughter, Joe Alt & Cole Strange protect DJ Uiagalelei (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Christian Barmore and New England Patriots's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
